items.originalQuestion: Does a rug edge obstruct the walking route?
items.question: Is a rug or mat edge visibly raised, curled, or bunched on a walking path in this photo, where someone could trip?
items.relevanceQuestion: Is a rug or floor mat visible on a walking path in this photo?
items.limitation: A photo does not establish whether a rug is secured or whether the route is used.

items.originalQuestion: Does a cord cross the walking route?
items.question: Is a visible loose cord or cable crossing an open floor area used as a walking path in this photo?
items.relevanceQuestion: Is an open floor walking path visible in this photo?
items.limitation: The visible path and cable may be partly occluded; actual use is unknown.

items.originalQuestion: Do objects obstruct the sample stairs?
items.question: Are loose objects visibly occupying a stair tread or the walking area of a stair landing in this photo?
items.relevanceQuestion: Are stairs or a stair landing visible in this photo?
items.limitation: This covers visible steps only, not the entire staircase.

items.originalQuestion: Is the sample stair handrail loose?
items.question: Does a visible stair handrail have an obvious break, detached bracket, or visibly separated wall or floor attachment in this photo?
items.relevanceQuestion: Is a stair handrail and at least one of its attachment points visible in this photo?
items.limitation: Visible damage is a proxy. A single photo cannot test looseness or load capacity.

items.originalQuestion: Is a light or accessible switch missing for the sample stairs?
items.question: Are visible stair treads or a stair landing so dimly lit in this photo that their edges are difficult to distinguish?
items.relevanceQuestion: Are stairs or a stair landing visible in this photo?
items.limitation: Exposure affects apparent brightness. A photo cannot establish missing lighting, switch accessibility, or normal lighting conditions.

items.originalQuestion: Is the sample route from bed to bathroom dark?
items.question: Is a visible walking path beside a bed or through a bedroom doorway so dimly lit in this photo that floor obstacles would be difficult to see?
items.relevanceQuestion: Is a bed with an adjoining floor walking path, or a bedroom doorway and its walking path, visible in this photo?
items.limitation: A single photo cannot establish a bed-to-bathroom route or its nighttime lighting.

items.originalQuestion: Is the sample shower surface described as slippery?
items.question: Is pooled water, a visibly wet glossy patch, or a loose bunched mat visible on a bathtub or shower floor in this photo?
items.relevanceQuestion: Is the floor or standing surface of a bathtub or shower visible in this photo?
items.limitation: Visible wetness or a loose mat is a proxy. A photo cannot measure friction or determine slipperiness.

items.originalQuestion: Is support reported as missing where needed near the sample tub or toilet?
items.question: Is a bathtub, shower, or toilet and its adjoining wall visible in this photo with no grab bar visible beside that fixture?
items.relevanceQuestion: Is a bathtub, shower, or toilet together with its adjoining wall visible in this photo?
items.limitation: An out-of-frame bar may exist. A photo cannot determine a person's support needs or whether a bar is properly installed.
